tb-501-1.question:
A doctor places a radioactive source in a person’s body for medical check-up. The radiation emitted should have a weak ionizing power to minimize the damage caused to the person. Which of the following sources is the most suitable?

A α source

B β source

C γ source

D They are equally suitable.
tb-501-1.reasoning: γ radiation has the weakest ionizing power and the strongest penetrating power. It is relatively less harmful.

tb-501-2.question:
Jacky sets up a diffusion cloud chamber. The observation is as shown in Figure a.

At point P,

A ionizing radiation is emitted.

B ionizing radiation is stopped.

C ions are formed.

D ions are absorbed.
tb-501-2.reasoning: Alcohol vapour condenses and form tiny alcohol droplets around the ions.

tb-501-3.question:
Which of the following statements about X-rays and γ radiation is incorrect?

A Both are ionizing radiation.

B Both are electromagnetic radiation.

C Both are spontaneously emitted from unstable nuclei.

D Both carry no charge.
tb-501-3.reasoning: γ radiation is spontaneously emitted from unstable nuclei while X-ray is emitted when fast electrons hit a heavy metal target.

tb-501-4.question:
In a laboratory, a GM counter is placed on a clear bench and it records a non-zero count rate. Which of the following is a possible source of the radiation detected by the counter?

A Radioactive source used for experiments

B Cosmic rays from outer space

C Walls of the laboratory

D All of the above

tb-501-5.question:
A right-angled fork track is formed when an α source is placed in a cloud chamber filled with helium gas. What conclusion can be drawn?

A An α particle is positively charged.

B An α particle has the same mass as a helium nucleus.

C An α particle consists of two protons and two neutrons.

D The ionizing power of α radiation is the strongest among nuclear radiations.

tb-501-6.question:
Daisy uses a GM counter to study a radioactive source. The background count rate is measured to be about 29 min–1. When she places the source 10 cm from the GM tube, the count rate increases to 132 min–1. Which of the following statements is correct?

A The source emits α radiation only.

B The source emits α radiation and β radiation.

C The source does not emit α radiation.

D She cannot tell if the source emits α radiation.
tb-501-6.reasoning: The range of α radiation in air is only a few centimetres. α radiation emitted by the source cannot reach the GM tube.

tb-501-7.question:
A radioactive source is placed very close to a GM tube which is connected to a counter. Different absorbers are placed in turn between the source and the GM tube (Fig b).

The count rates measured for different absorbers are recorded in Table a.

What type(s) of radiation does the source emit?

A α only

tb-501-7.reasoning:

tb-501-8.question:
Which of the following actions can reduce the exposure to ionizing radiation?

(1) Exercise often

(2) Avoid unnecessary X-ray scan

(3) Maintain good ventilation in an indoor environment

A (2) only

B (3) only

C (1) and (2) only

D (2) and (3) only
tb-501-8.reasoning:
Good ventilation in an indoor environment prevents radon gas from accumulating.

∴ (3) is correct.

tb-501-9.question:
An α source is placed between two conducting plates (Fig c).

The pointer of the galvanometer deflects. Which of the following statements is/are correct?

(1) A current is detected because α particles are attracted to one of the plates.

(2) No current will be detected if the set-up is placed in a vacuum.

(3) If the α source is replaced with a β source, the current flowing through the circuit is likely to be smaller.

A (2) only

B (1) and (3) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-501-9.reasoning:
The current detected is caused by the ions produced by α radiation, rather than the α particles.

∴ (1) is incorrect.

No ions are produced if the set-up is placed in a vacuum.

∴ (2) is correct.

β radiation has a weaker ionizing power than α radiation and therefore produces less ions.

∴ (3) is correct.

tb-501-10.question:
A β source is placed in front of a uniform magnetic field pointing into page. Maximum reading is recorded by the GM tube at the position shown in Figure d. If the β source is replaced by an α source, at which position would the GM tube record a maximum reading?

A P

B Q

C R

D S
tb-501-10.reasoning: α radiation is deflected in the opposite direction to a smaller extent.

tb-501-11.question:
Which of the following statements about detectors of nuclear radiation is/are correct?

(1) A GM counter can detect background radiation.

(2) Due to background radiation, tracks can be observed even if there is no radioactive source in a cloud chamber.

(3) A photographic film wrapped in thick paper can be used to detect any type of nuclear radiation.

A (1) only

B (1) and (2) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-501-11.reasoning:
A photographic film wrapped in thick paper cannot detect α radiation since α radiation can be stopped by thick paper.

∴ (3) is incorrect.

tb-501-12.question:
The following set-up is used to investigate the deflection of β radiation in a uniform magnetic field (Fig e). A GM tube connected to a counter measures the count rate as it moves along arc PQ.

Which of the following correctly shows the graphs of the corrected count rate R against θ when the magnetic field is in place (blue line) and not in place (orange line)?
tb-501-12.reasoning:
When the magnetic field is not in place, β radiation moves in straight line. A peak is detected by the GM tube at M (θ = 90°).

When the magnetic field is in place, β radiation is deflected downwards. A peak is detected by the GM tube at some point along arc MQ
(θ > 90°).

tb-501-17.question: In a physics lesson, your teacher gives you a pure β source and asks you to verify that β particles are negatively charged by using the apparatus shown in Figure h. Describe the procedures of the experiment with the aid of suitable diagrams and state the expected results. (7 marks)
tb-501-17.answer:
(Correct setup) 1A

Put away the source and measure the background count rate. 1A

Put the source a few centimetres in front of the GM tube. At a position between the GM tube and the source, arrange the lead sheets side by side and leave a narrow gap in front of the source. 1A

Compare the count rate at X with the background count rate, there should be an increase in count rate. 1A

Then, put the magnets between the lead sheets and the GM tube, producing a magnetic field pointing downwards. 1A

The count rate at X should drop to a similar level as the background count rate. 1A

Move the GM tube sideways along PQ. There should be a position (Y) along XQ where the count rate is higher than the background count rate. This shows that β particles are negatively charged. 1A

tb-501-18.question:
Radiation workers are required to wear film badges to monitor their exposure to radiation.

A film wrapped in paper is embedded in the badge. Aluminium and lead sheets are also placed inside the badge (Fig i).

The films worn by two workers, Ben and Collin, are developed. The degree of blackening on different regions of the films is shown in Table c.

Region on the film

Degree of blackening Ben

Degree of blackening Collin

Beneath open window

5

4

Beneath aluminium sheet

3

4

Beneath lead sheet

0

3

Note: 0 = not blackened, 5 = most blackened

Table c

(a) Why is the film wrapped? (1 mark)

(b) From the above data, explain whether Ben and Collin are definitely exposed to α, β or γ radiation. (6 marks)
tb-501-18.answer:
(a) The film is wrapped to block visible light. 1A

(b) Since α radiation cannot penetrate the paper wrapping the film, 1A

we cannot deduce whether they are exposed to α radiation. 1A

For Ben, the region beneath the 5-mm lead sheet is not blackened. This shows that Ben is not exposed to γ radiation. 1A

tb-501-19.question:
A radioactive source emitting α and β radiations is placed in front of the two conducting plates that are connected to a power supply. The radiations split into two streams X and Y as they travel between the plates (Fig j).

(a) State the nature of α and β radiation. (2 marks)

(b) (i) What types of nuclear radiation are X and Y? Explain briefly. (4 marks)

(ii) State the polarities of terminals A and B. (1 mark)

(iii) The electric field is then replaced with a magnetic field. The radiation splits in a similar way as shown in Figure j in the magnetic field. What is the direction of the magnetic field? (1 mark)
tb-501-19.answer:
(a) α radiation is a stream of positively charged helium nuclei. 1A

β radiation is a stream of negatively charged fast-moving electrons. 1A

(b) (i) X is β radiation and 1A

Y is α radiation. 1A

The mass to charge ratio of an α particle is much larger than that of a β particle, 1A

so α radiation has a much smaller deflection in an electric field. 1A

(ii) A: positive, B: negative 1A

(iii) Out of the page 1A

Pigment

black

carbon

white

lead

tb-501-22.question:
A radioactive source R is put in front of two oppositely charged parallel metal plates (Fig m).

A GM tube is placed 15 cm away from R. The count rates at X, Y and Z are recorded.

Then the metal plates are removed, and the count rates are recorded again. The graphs below show the results (Figs n-p).

(a) Estimate the background count rate. (1 mark)

(b) Can we determine whether R emits α radiation? Explain briefly. (2 marks)

(c) Explain which kind of nuclear radiation makes the count rate at X increase in the presence of the metal plates. (2 marks)

(d) Estimate the count rates due to (i) β radiation and (ii) γ radiation at Y when the plates are removed. (2 marks)
tb-501-22.answer:
(a) 60 min–1 (Accept 55 to 65 min–1) 1A

(b) No. 1A

The range of α radiation is much shorter than the distance between R and the GM tube. 1A

As a result, no α radiation can be recorded. 1A

(c) Some radiation is deflected to X in the presence of the metal plates. 1A

Since α radiation cannot be detected, the increase in count rate is due to β radiation. 1A

(d) Refer to Figure o.

(i) Count rate due to β radiation

= 210 – 140

= 70 min–1 1A

(ii) Count rate due to γ radiation

= 140 – background count rate

= 140 – 60

= 80 min–1 1A
